quick: With or without food (high-fat meal lowers Cmax)
Caution in severe impairment; avoid volume depletion
Contraindicated in severe hepatic impairment / cholestasis
summary: Fimasartan is a selective angiotensin II type-1 (AT1) receptor blocker approved in South Korea and some other countries (not US FDA-approved) for essential hypertension. The usual dose is 60 mg once daily (range 30-120 mg). Like other ARBs it carries class risks of fetal toxicity (contraindicated in pregnancy), hyperkalemia, hypotension and renal dysfunction, and dual RAAS blockade should be avoided. It is generally well tolerated, with headache and dizziness the commonest effects.
indications: Treatment of essential (mild to moderate) hypertension, alone or in combination with other antihypertensive agents

dosage.n: Antihypertensive effect within 2 weeks; full effect by 8-12 weeks

dosage.d: May increase to 120 mg/day or decrease to 30 mg/day per response
Consider 30 mg once daily and correct volume first
Available with hydrochlorothiazide or amlodipine in fixed-dose products

admin: Take orally once daily at about the same time each day
May be taken with or without food; a high-fat meal reduces peak concentration but is acceptable
Do not use potassium supplements or potassium-containing salt substitutes without advice
Stop and seek advice immediately if pregnancy occurs
Maintain consistent dosing for steady blood pressure control
moa: Fimasartan selectively and competitively blocks the angiotensin II type-1 (AT1) receptor, preventing angiotensin II-mediated vasoconstriction and aldosterone release. This lowers peripheral vascular resistance and blood pressure without inhibiting ACE, so it does not increase bradykinin and is less likely to cause cough.

absolute: Severe hepatic impairment, biliary obstruction or cholestasis
Concomitant aliskiren in patients with diabetes or renal impairment
relative: Concurrent ACE inhibitor or aliskiren (dual RAAS blockade)
monitor: Pregnancy status in women of childbearing potential

preg: Drugs acting on the renin-angiotensin system can cause fetal injury and death in the second and third trimesters (oligohydramnios, renal failure, hypotension, skull hypoplasia). Fimasartan is contraindicated in pregnancy; discontinue as soon as pregnancy is detected.
lact: It is not known whether fimasartan is excreted in human milk. Because of potential risk to the infant, use during breastfeeding is not recommended.
renal: Use with caution in renal impairment; correct volume depletion before starting and monitor potassium and renal function. Risk of acute renal dysfunction in renal artery stenosis or severe heart failure.
hepatic: Fimasartan is eliminated largely via the hepatobiliary route. It is contraindicated in severe hepatic impairment, biliary obstruction and cholestasis; use cautiously in mild-to-moderate impairment.

major: Aliskiren in diabetes/renal impairment - contraindicated (hyperkalemia, hypotension, renal impairment)
ACE inhibitors (dual RAAS blockade) - increased renal impairment and hyperkalemia
moderate: NSAIDs - reduced antihypertensive effect and increased renal/hyperkalemia risk
Lithium - increased lithium concentrations and toxicity
Other antihypertensives/diuretics - additive blood pressure lowering
interactions.food: May be taken with or without food; high-fat meals reduce Cmax. Avoid potassium-rich salt substitutes.
interactions.alcohol: Alcohol may add to blood-pressure lowering; advise moderation.
interactions.diagnostics: May raise serum potassium and creatinine; affects renin-aldosterone testing.

monitoring: Serum potassium and renal function at baseline and periodically
Pregnancy status in women of childbearing potential
counsel: Take once daily at the same time, with or without food
Tell your doctor immediately if you become pregnant
Rise slowly when starting treatment to avoid dizziness
Avoid potassium-containing salt substitutes unless advised
Report swelling of the face, lips or throat right away
pk: Blood-pressure lowering within hours; sustained over 24 h
Store at 20-25 C; protect from moisture and light
pearls: NOT FDA-approved - approved in South Korea (and some other markets) for essential hypertension; this record is based on Korean MFDS/manufacturer prescribing information and ARB-class data, not an FDA label
Selective AT1 blocker: lower cough/angioedema risk than ACE inhibitors but class fetal toxicity applies
Eliminated mainly hepatobiliary - contraindicated in severe hepatic impairment/cholestasis, an important difference from many ARBs
Avoid dual RAAS blockade (with ACE inhibitor or aliskiren)
Onset of full antihypertensive effect may take up to 8-12 weeks
missed: Take the missed dose as soon as you remember. If it is almost time for the next dose, skip the missed dose and resume the usual schedule. Do not take two doses at once.
overdose: The most likely manifestation is hypotension (with possible tachycardia or reflex bradycardia). Management is supportive: place the patient supine and give intravenous fluids to expand volume. Fimasartan is unlikely to be removed by dialysis. Monitor blood pressure, potassium and renal function.
